findings.title: User-controlled groupBy reaches raw GROUP BY clause
findings.description: The groupBy query parameter of the CSV export is forwarded to buildQuery(), which concatenates it into the GROUP BY clause. A clinic administrator can alter the export query and pull rows from other clinics' appointment and billing tables.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy header configured
findings.description: next.config.ts defines no headers() block, so every page is served without a Content-Security-Policy. Any script injection in the portal would run with full access to the patient session.

findings.title: Sessions never expire server-side
findings.description: Session records have no expiry and are not revoked when a patient changes their password, so a stolen session stays valid indefinitely.

findings.title: FHIR import fetches arbitrary server URLs
findings.description: The FHIR import endpoint fetches a server URL supplied by the clinic admin without restricting the destination. It can be pointed at internal services such as the cloud metadata endpoint.

findings.title: Phone number regex vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking
findings.description: The phone validator uses a nested-quantifier pattern that backtracks exponentially on long inputs. A single crafted sign-up request can pin a server CPU for several seconds.

findings.cweName: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
findings.title: Appointment API returns the provider's internal notes
findings.description: The appointment response serializes the full database row, including the provider's internal notes field that the UI never displays. Patients can read clinician notes by inspecting the API response.
